versions.name: RXV2-0.9.737-one-installer
versions.notes: Only one piece of code installs an update now (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'we seem to have multiple places that install updates. One gives byte count, one does not. I suggest only one bit of code should update so we only ever need to update that bit'). The front page carried its own copy, which had drifted: no byte count, no choice of WiFi or Bluetooth, no three-minute grace before calling an install failed, and a different failure message. Its 'Update now?' offer now opens the update page and installs from there - 117 lines of duplicate gone, and the one remaining installer is the better one. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.736-tuning-backup
versions.notes: Both Back up steps in the Tuning wizard went to Setup instead of the backup page (Malcolm 2026-09-17). The same fault was fixed in the New helicopter wizard in 0.9.687 and the Tuning one was missed. Both now open Back up. New check: every internal link on every page must lead to a page that exists, AND a wizard step called 'Back up' must lead to the backup page - the wrong-page half is what a plain link checker cannot see. Publishing refuses if either fails. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.735-backup-message
versions.notes: Back up said 'connect to the receiver first' on a dongle (Malcolm 2026-09-17). Two things were wrong with that sentence: it said receiver when it was a dongle, and it was not the reason - the only thing that refuses a backup there is the demo. It now says 'this is the demo - nothing here is really connected' when that is why, and 'connect to the receiver or dongle first' when nothing is connected. Same for Restore and for importing a backup file, on both phones.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.734-dongle-words
versions.notes: The pages called it a receiver even when it is a dongle (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'item 2 says Receiver even when it's a dongle... yes this also affects Wiring and many others'). Now, on a dongle: Before you start step 2 says dongle throughout, tells you to choose 'dongle on a wire' rather than 'receiver', and says to use port B or C and leave port A alone - that is usually the receiver's, and the receiver is what flies the model; its no-USB-cable route sets MSP for the dongle's port instead of serial receiver for the receiver's. The Wiring page's last card was the worst of them: it told you to plug into the receiver's port, which would take the port the model flies on - it now says port B or C, not the receiver's, and how to set it. Elsewhere a shared list of phrases corrects the wording (the WiFi page's 'receiver's own WiFi', the log's 'everything the receiver noticed', 'Rename receiver'), deliberately leaving alone the places where 'receiver' is right: Rotorflight's own 'serial receiver' port function, the configurator's Receiver tab, and 'the receiver that flies the model'. The one-page guide and the wiring page now say port B or C, never A. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.732-button-spacing
versions.notes: The four round buttons at the top (home, back, search, help) overlapped slightly on Android (Malcolm's Pixel): their positions were set in em, and the web view's base font is 16 px on Android but about 14 px on iPhone, so the middle two grew inward until they touched. They are now placed in fixed pixels, the same on both. Pages only; nothing else changes.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.731-after-update
versions.notes: Two things Malcolm noticed right after installing 0.9.730 over WiFi from the app, both explained by the receiver's own log. 1) 'It hesitated worryingly at the end': the phone reconnected 1.5 s after the reboot, and the receiver began its WiFi join at 2.4 s - the join and the phone's Bluetooth polls starved each other, the first 25 s attempt failed, WiFi was up only at 31 s, and the update page crawled through that window. An update asked for from the app now holds the WiFi join for 20 s after the reboot so the phone can confirm on a quiet radio; AP, web and Bluetooth come up at once as before. The receiver also keeps its log across an update reboot now, so a first attempt that stalls leaves its story behind. 2) 'Bluetooth is the only way - no WiFi here', moments after a WiFi update: the page read 'still joining' as 'none'. It now says the receiver is joining WiFi after its restart, and re-checks by itself. 3) The Ports page showed UART numbers but not the Nexus letters (Malcolm): a Nexus-X flashed with the NEXUS_F7 config reports 'NEXUS_F7', which the page did not recognise. Any Nexus now gets Port A/B/C (the same UARTs on every Nexus), and the page shows the board name it was given.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.730-dongle-review
versions.notes: Before two dongles go to a stranger: five independent reviews of the whole dongle path (first contact, byte-level correctness of every Rotorflight read and write, the dongle in a flying model, the phone apps over Bluetooth, and the guide against reality), every finding checked in the code before it was fixed. Nothing changes in the air for a receiver. What was fixed: the receiver now says 'No flight controller is answering' at once instead of waiting 8 s per read; a synchronous flight-controller wait was still pumping control frames into a dongle's MSP port (now guarded twice over); a WiFi retry scheduled just before arming could switch the WiFi radio back on for the whole flight (now cleared by the teardown); a dongle's armed word is now asked four times a second, 'no fresh word' is never taken as 'disarmed', and every write, save, restart and reboot a dongle can be asked for needs a fresh 'disarmed' from the flight controller; a dongle never rewrites another model's telemetry sensors, never blind-restarts a silent flight controller, never sleeps on a low battery, never opens the raw MSP bridge, and never reads a radio it has not got; three reboots that skipped the USB close (factory reset, first-run, WiFi) now close it; the Rotorflight hub no longer says 'connected' with nothing answering; Easy tuning could wrap a rate over 1275 deg/s into a wrong byte and 'verify' it; a blank Servos box was written as 0 us; PID+ showed a control Rotorflight 4.6 hard-codes; PID spool-up now covers all 6 banks; the dongle page saved ports with the OLD speed over Bluetooth; the front page recovers by itself after a reboot; the welcome card and help now speak of a dongle. Apps 5.68 (iOS) / 5.61 (Android): a backup from another model no longer carries its pilot's channel map or selector channels; timeouts reach pages as one plain line, not a web page; a refused update says the receiver's own sentence and offers a way back; Bluetooth update transfers get the time they need; Android now shows the pages' plain dialogs (rename worked on iPhone only) and no longer loops when Bluetooth is off; iPhone notices Bluetooth being switched on and reconnects by identity, not by name. The one-page guide and the wiring page were rewritten: the 5 V rule, Nexus port order, how the app really connects, and where the iPhone app stands.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.729-landing-manners
versions.notes: Three things from Malcolm's four test flights (2026-09-16, zero crashes). 1) The servo wiggle waited for 'head speed zero' - but that number is the motor's, and on a helicopter the motor stops the instant the throttle is cut while the head coasts on for ~20 s: the tail 'waggled like an excited puppy' on a turning rotor. The wiggle now waits 20 s from the last reading that showed the head turning, and never comes inside 5 s of the safety switch going on. A plain power-up keeps its prompt boot wiggle. 2) Long gaps in the transmitter's log right after the safety switch: on disarm, bringing Bluetooth (and at home, WiFi) back stalled the receiver with no warning to the transmitter, so it was logged as a real gap; on arm, the warning was sent in a 50 ms burst the transmitter can miss while it is writing its own log. Every such pause now announces itself and waits until the transmitter has actually taken the message before it happens. 3) Two wiggles for the price of one: with the transmitter on at power-up, the 30 s Bluetooth boot window closed and auto fly mode switched it straight back on, with a second wiggle. When the model is disarmed it now simply stays up; arming turns it off as before. Firmware only; nothing changes in the air (all of this runs disarmed, on the ground).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.728-wifi-heal
versions.notes: Fixes WiFi going dead after an app session (Malcolm 2026-09-15: two receivers unreachable over WiFi until a power-cycle). With Bluetooth connected, the shared radio must let WiFi sleep, and a busy Bluetooth link can starve it until it stops hearing the router - yet it still reports itself connected, so it never tried to rejoin. Now, the moment the app disconnects, the receiver re-syncs its WiFi by itself. No more power-cycle to get it back. Safe by construction: this only runs on the ground - WiFi is off in the air - and never while a transmitter link is live or the model is armed. Firmware only; pages and apps unchanged from 0.9.727.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.727-preflight-gates
versions.notes: Pre-flight safety check (Malcolm: 'check that none of our code edits is going to interfere with control of the model when it's in the air'). Today's edits could not: the receiver's firmware was unchanged since the reviewed 0.9.715, the apps' own code was unchanged, and the pages only asked for two read-only things. In the air, WiFi and Bluetooth are off anyway - they switch off 0.8 s after arming, locked on with Rotorflight. The check did find four older paths that could restart the receiver or write an update with no transmitter or armed check, which 0.9.715 had given to their siblings: a Bluetooth update now needs the transmitter off (as a WiFi update already did); renaming and Reboot need it off and the model disarmed; the reboot at the end of a Bluetooth update is refused while armed. Renaming now restarts the safe way (throttle-low frames, output parked) instead of a bare restart. And a dongle no longer sends ~100 ms of control frames into the flight controller's MSP port when it restarts.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.726-page-fix
versions.notes: Fixes the Check-for-Update screen, which stayed blank in 0.9.725 - the page's script had a missing catch block, so nothing on it ran. Withdrawn: 0.9.725 is no longer offered. Also carries what 0.9.725 meant to: far fewer words on screen (Malcolm: 'too many words - the explanations can be in the help screens, this is true across the whole app'). Nothing is lost - every explanation moved into that page's ? help, in full. About 1000 words came off the pages: the update page (install-over choice, progress line, failure message, and release notes now clipped to two lines, tap for the rest), Receiver settings, WiFi, Dongle, the welcome and bind panels on the front page, and Travel extents. Safety and consequence lines stay, cut to one sentence. The step-by-step guides keep their words. New: every page's script is now parse-checked before anything can be published.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.724-teal-check
versions.notes: The Check for a Rotorflight update button was grey, which reads as disabled (Malcolm spotted it). It is now teal with an icon, like the buttons above it. The demo now answers the check properly too - its flight controller is a real 4.6.0, so it says 'up to date' as a real receiver would, instead of 'could not check' on a phone that plainly has internet.
